_help: Completed V3 channel style derived from the primary Britain We Lived In reference. Keep the keys stable when importing it into the tool.
name: Britain We Lived In
audience: Primarily British viewers aged 45+ and the British diaspora who remember post-war school dinners, family food, high streets, household routines and vanished brands; secondarily younger viewers interested in everyday British social history.

use_for: British nostalgia tone and visual sourcing
bold yellow-and-white key-phrase captions with black outline
red brush-stroke emphasis used selectively in the hook
full-screen chapter cards with a framed subject image, dark brown grid, gold particles and purple/yellow paint stroke
hard-cut pacing, food close-ups and contextual archival photographs
chapter structure and restrained nostalgic music

topic_inheritance.rule: Keep the channel's editing language consistent while selecting visuals, facts and archival material specifically for each script.

pacing._help: How long one visual stays on screen (seconds).
slow_down_on: the last line of an item
pacing._rule: General rule (all channels): a sentence up to 7 s = one clip; longer = split into parts of 3-7 s, each from a DIFFERENT video; no clip under 3 s after the hook; cuts only at sentence/phrase boundaries so clips stay in sync with the voice.

structure._help: What each part of the video must do.

hook.first_shot: An immediately recognisable authentic British period shot tied to the premise: for food videos use a school dinner serving line, dinner ladies, pupils at tables or a close-up of the most nostalgic dish; start on action, not a logo or title slate.
hook._if_no_hook: General rule: if the script has no hook, the video starts directly at Item 1.

chapter_card.when: only where the script has an item heading
chapter_card.style: Full-screen V3 reference chapter card: near-black/dark-brown grid background with restrained gold particles; one large rounded-corner subject image centred in the upper two-thirds; a rough purple paint stroke with a smaller yellow edge across the lower image; bold condensed white uppercase title with a heavy black outline. Animate with a quick image scale-in and title pop; never show a plain text-only slate.

each_item.first_shot: The chapter card's strong finished-item image, followed by a clean close-up or serving shot of the exact item; for non-food topics use the exact product, place or object named in the heading.
each_item.ingredients_card: When the script lists ingredients, show one V3 bold ingredient card: dark-brown grid background, large central bowl or finished-dish image, 3-6 ingredient cutouts or small framed photos, short white labels with yellow quantities, purple/red brush accents, and no scrapbook, chalkboard or cursive treatment.
each_item.story_lines: shots of the same dish (being made or served)
each_item.history_lines: period photos or period footage of the dish if they exist, else the dish
each_item.last_shot: finished dish or people enjoying it

subscribe_reminder.when: once after the hook and once in the outro only
subscribe_reminder.style: small channel button; never cover the food

outro.show: End on the strongest finished-item or authentic period memory shot, add one brief viewer-memory question in the V3 comment-card style, then a small subscribe reminder and a short warm fade to black; do not use a long logo animation.

scene_rules._help: What to show for each KIND of sentence. The tool picks the first rule that matches.

rules.when_sentence_has: a route, movement between places, or a location essential to understanding the story
a place or region mentioned only as background context
rules.show: relevant footage or archival photo; do not automatically show a map

rules.when_sentence_has: a span of years (e.g. '1950s to the 1980s')

rules.show: clip of exactly that step if found, else the dish being made
period photo or home-movie style footage
a fading family recipe card, closed cookbook, empty serving plate, or period photo; avoid unrelated empty shelves
verified archival packaging or a neutral dish shot; never generate a logo

rules.when_sentence_has: a number, ranking, temperature, duration, or quantity
rules.show: a short readable fact graphic only when the number is important

footage._help: Where visuals come from, in the order the tool tries them.
footage.on_insufficient_real_footage: mark item as needs_footage and block automatic final export; do not silently fill the item with AI images
footage._note: For British dishes, brands and daily life, prefer licensed or usage-approved material from British Pathé, the BFI National Archive, Huntley Film Archives, Imperial War Museums and BBC Archive, plus verified UK museum or council archives. Do not assume that public viewing equals permission for automated reuse.

visual_mix._help: Target mix for a normal completed item. The validator may allow small changes when authentic material is scarce.

repetition._help: Stops the video from feeling repetitive.
repetition._rule: General rule (all channels): the same moment of a source never twice in the whole video; never loop a clip.

photos.motion: slow push-in or pan; never static
photos.frame: full-screen; product photos may use a clean cutout on a deep red, magenta, cream, or dark neutral background; no scrapbook or polaroid frame

never_show._help: Anything here is refused by the clip checker.
people: recognisable AI face repeated with inconsistent identity
places: modern kitchen when the shot claims to be historical
American diner, American school cafeteria or US suburban kitchen when the narration is about a British home or school
non-British school uniforms, packaging, road signs or currency presented as British
modern supermarket aisle when the line specifically describes a vanished British high-street shop
other: a different dish than the item
American version of a British dish (e.g. US biscuits for British biscuits)

motion_graphics._help: Graphics allowed on this channel and how often. Designs must exist in the library; missing ones are reported, never faked.
wanted_but_missing: v3_bold_paint_chapter: dark-brown grid, gold particles, rounded subject image, purple/yellow brush stroke and outlined white title
v3_bold_ingredient_grid: ingredient cutouts with yellow quantities and white names
v3_brush_fact: large yellow/white number or phrase over a red or purple rough paint stroke
v3_memory_quote: viewer-memory quote or question with an archival photo
v3_product_cutout: isolated package or object on the dark grid background

look._help: Colour and texture of the whole video.
look.grain: Subtle fine grain, approximately 6-10% on modern footage and up to 15% on restored archive material; never obscure food detail or text.
look.colour: Warm, slightly faded 1960s-1980s British colour with gentle amber highlights and restrained saturation; archival black-and-white stays neutral, while food remains appetising and clear.
look.vignette: Subtle 6-10% edge darkening on chapter cards, photos and generated graphics; little or none on already-dark archive footage.

transitions._help: How one shot changes to the next.
transitions.default: Hard cut; use a 4-8 frame dissolve only for an emotional archival-photo change or entry into a chapter card.
transitions.into_chapter_card: hard cut or very short dissolve; never insert an empty frame

captions.position: middle for major hook/fact phrases; bottom for secondary phrases, always inside safe margins
captions.animation: fast pop with a slight overshoot; selected keywords may receive a left-to-right brush highlight
captions.font: Impact for major phrases and chapter titles; Montserrat ExtraBold fallback for longer captions
captions.colour: White text with a heavy black outline; one important word or phrase in bright yellow #FFE234; red #D52B2B or purple #5A43F5 rough brush backing only for selected emphasis
captions.case: Title Case for key phrases; UPPERCASE only for chapter titles, one-word emphasis and major numbers
captions.mode: Key facts, sensory phrases and memorable lines only; denser in the hook, selective in the body

text.long_text: shrink then wrap to two lines, never cut

highlight_word.style: Turn the most important 1-4 words bright yellow while the remaining phrase stays white; use a thick black outline and optional rough red/purple paint stroke, never a solid subtitle box.

text.key_phrase_pop_ups: Every 4-7 seconds during the first 30-second hook, then approximately every 12-20 seconds or at a genuine emotional/factual beat; never caption every sentence.
text.cursive_rule: Never for captions, chapter titles or ingredient labels; a tiny cursive signature may appear only inside an authentic scanned recipe card.
text.source_label: Not used on ordinary footage; a small unobtrusive archive credit may be shown only when the licence requires it.

ai_images._help: Only when nothing real exists. Prompts follow these rules.
ai_images.look: match the script's era as a real period photograph of the FOOD; British home, not American
ai_images.people: General rule (all channels): NO people. Never women/families standing in a kitchen, never a full-kitchen wide shot. At most hands at work.

checker._help: Extra rules the AI checker applies to every clip, besides 'never_show'.
reject_if: a person doing something unrelated (opening drawers, walking)
a very dark / nearly black shot
accept_if: the exact cooking action matches the narration
a clean appetising shot of the correct dish supports a non-procedural line
a verified period image supports a historical claim
warn_if: the same source dominates more than 20 seconds
the same composition appears three times in ten scenes
a historical claim is illustrated only by generated imagery

quality_gates._help: Final automatic checks before the video may be exported.
block_export_if: an item has no real video and no approved exception
real video share for an item is below 0.65
a selected clip shows the wrong dish
a historical scene contains an obvious modern device
generated imagery contains a brand logo
a caption is clipped, outside safe margins, or below minimum size
a transition contains a blank frame
the same few seconds of a clip loop/repeat
quality_gates.approved_exception_requires: a saved reason plus manual approval for genuinely unavailable archival subjects

parallel_processing._help: Bounded concurrency for speed without increasing provider blocks.

sound._help: Not used by the tool yet; written down for later.
sound.music: Warm, understated British nostalgia: soft piano, celesta, brushed percussion and light strings, with a gentle 1960s-1970s documentary feel. Keep it well below the voice-over, lift briefly into chapter cards, avoid vocals, comedy music, aggressive trailer drums and sentimental over-scoring.
sound.sound_effects: subtle whoosh or impact on major yellow fact overlays and quiet archival texture where appropriate; no page-turn scrapbook effects or cartoon pops
